Usage assumptions (per hour)
Define how your users behave during an average and peak hour. These inputs shape the base demand before modelling the full day.
column4:
Derived metrics
Calculated values that describe your expected demand profile.

column1:
Average users per active hour

The typical number of users active in a non-peak hour. Used to estimate baseline API/Genie load.
column4:
Average concurrent users
The estimated number of users simultaneously active at any given moment during a typical hour. Calculated from: (Average users per hour × Average session duration) / 60

column1:
Peak users in busiest hour
The maximum number of users active in the busiest hour of the day (your highest concurrency). Determines peak QPM.
column4:
Peak concurrent users
The maximum number of users simultaneously active during the busiest hour of the day. This determines your theoretical peak demand before scaling by interaction behaviour.

column1:
Average visit duration (minutes)
How long a typical user session lasts. Longer sessions → more concurrent usage.

Adoption rate (%)
The percentage of your total population that actually uses the system each hour. Helps scale down large user counts realistically.
column4:
Avg QPM (selected scenario)
The average number of queries per minute generated during normal load based on your selected interaction style.

column1:
Number of peaks per weekday (1, 2, or 3 supported)
How many traffic spikes your application has per day (e.g., 1 = midday; 2 = morning + afternoon; 3 = morning + noon + evening). Shapes the daily demand curve.
column4:
Peak QPM (selected scenario)
The expected number of queries per minute during the busiest period of the day, reflecting both peak concurrency and interaction speed.

column1:
Peak width (hours)
Controls how sharp or wide each peak is. Smaller values = sharper spikes. Larger values = broader, flatter peaks.

Interaction behaviour
Control how quickly your users issue queries. Scenarios affect overall QPM load.
column4:
For chosen QPM reservation
Shows how your selected reservation performs under your traffic model.

column1:
Chosen scenario
Selects a predefined interaction style (Fast, Standard, Slow).
column4:
% queries queued
The percentage of total daily queries that exceed your reserved QPM capacity and must wait (i.e., should be put in a queue).

column1:
Selected time per query (seconds)
Automatically filled based on the chosen scenario.
Represents how long an average interaction takes → affects QPM.
column4:
% time above cap
The percentage of the day during which demand exceeds your reserved QPM.

Average utilisation
How much of your reserved QPM is actually used on average across the entire day (weekday + weekend).
